content: Caspase recruitment domains (CARDs) are specialized protein interaction motifs that are predominantly found in proteins involved in inflammation and apoptosis. These domains facilitate the assembly of larger protein complexes through direct CARD-CARD interactions. CARD domains are present in a diverse array of proteins, including helicases, kinases, mitochondrial proteins, caspases, and other cytoplasmic factors. CARD domains belong to a structural family of protein motifs known as the death fold. This structural class is characterized by six to seven antiparallel alpha helices arranged around a hydrophobic core, with an outer surface composed of charged residues. Other motifs in this family include the pyrin domain (PYD), death domain (DD), and death effector domain (DED), all of which are primarily involved in regulating apoptosis and inflammatory responses. CARD domains were initially identified due to their role in regulating caspase activation and apoptosis. The six-helix structure of the CARD domain is evolutionarily conserved, with homologous structures observed in the ced-3 and ced-4 genes of Caenorhabditis elegans, where key components of the apoptotic machinery were first described. CARD domains are found in several pro-apoptotic proteins, including caspases 1, 4, 5, 9, and 15 in mammals. In the context of the mammalian immune response, CARD domains play a critical role in the processing of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and interleukin-18 (IL-18). For example, the NLR protein Ipaf-1 contains an N-terminal CARD domain, a nucleotide-binding domain, and C-terminal leucine-rich repeats (LRRs). These LRRs are thought to function similarly to those in Toll-like receptors. Ipaf-1 is activated by intracellular bacterial pathogens like Salmonella typhimurium or other stress signals. Upon activation, Ipaf-1 recruits the CARD-containing adapter protein ASC and caspase-1 through CARD-CARD interactions, forming a large protein complex known as the inflammasome. This complex facilitates the autoproteolytic activation of caspase-1, which subsequently processes pro-IL-1β and pro-IL-18 into their mature, biologically active forms. CARD domains are also involved in antiviral signaling. Proteins such as RIG-I and MDA5, which contain twin N-terminal CARD domains and C-terminal RNA helicase domains, recognize intracellular double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), a molecular signature of many viral genomes (e.g., paramyxoviruses, orthomyxoviruses, and rhabdoviruses). Upon binding to dsRNA, the CARD domains of RIG-I and MDA5 interact with the CARD motif of the mitochondrial adapter protein IPS-1 (also known as MAVS, VISA, or Cardif). Although the precise nature of the complex formed during viral detection remains unclear, these interactions are critical for initiating downstream antiviral signaling pathways. Dysregulation of CARD proteins has been implicated in autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. Constitutive activation of certain CARD proteins, either due to genetic mutations or persistent stress signals, can lead to chronic inflammation. For instance, gain-of-function mutations in the intracellular NOD2 protein are associated with an increased risk of Crohn's disease. Similarly, activating mutations in PYD-containing proteins such as cryopyrin (CIAS-1) and pyrin (MEFV) are linked to Muckle-Wells Syndrome and familial Mediterranean fever, respectively. The following is a list of proteins containing CARD domains, along with their associated functions or aliases: BIRC2 (C-IAP1): Baculoviral inhibitor of apoptosis repeat-containing protein 2. BIRC3 (C-IAP2): Baculoviral inhibitor of apoptosis repeat-containing protein 3. Caspase 1 (ICE): Involved in IL-1β processing. Caspase 2: Apoptosis-related cysteine peptidase. Caspase 4: Apoptosis-related cysteine peptidase. Caspase 5: Apoptosis-related cysteine peptidase. Caspase 9: Apoptosis-related cysteine peptidase. Caspase 12: Apoptosis-related cysteine peptidase. Caspase 13: Apoptosis-related cysteine peptidase. ICEBERG: Caspase-1 inhibitor. Pseudo-ICE (COP1): Dominant-negative inhibitor of caspase-1. MDA5 (IFIH1): Melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5. MAVS (Cardif): Mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein. CRADD (RAIDD): Caspase and RIP adapter with a death domain. RAIDD-2: Death adaptor molecule. RIG-I (DDX58): Retinoic acid-inducible gene 1 protein. RIPK2 (RICK kinase): Receptor-interacting serine-threonine kinase 2. Bcl10: B-cell lymphoma/leukemia 10 protein. BINCA (C9orf89): Bcl10-interacting CARD protein. CARD6: Caspase recruitment domain family member 6. CARD8 (CARDINAL): Caspase recruitment domain family member 8. CARD9: Caspase recruitment domain family member 9. CARD10 (CARMA3): Caspase recruitment domain family member 10. CARD11 (CARMA1): Caspase recruitment domain family member 11. CARD14 (CARMA2): Caspase recruitment domain family member 14. APAF1 (CED4): Apoptotic peptidase activating factor 1. GLAVA1 (GLAV1): Glavaris peptidase activating factor 1. IPAF (NLRC4): Ice protease-activating factor. NOD1: Nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-containing protein 1. NOD2: Nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-containing protein 2. NLRP1 (NALP1): NLR family, pyrin domain-containing protein 1. NOL3: Nucleolar protein 3 (apoptosis repressor with CARD domain). PYCARD (ASC): PYD and CARD domain-containing protein. IPS1: RIG-I and MDA5 adapter protein.
